transcript.text: theres water in the bottom of my frige under the salad draws, keeps comming back after i mop it up

Water pooling under the salad drawers that keeps returning usually means the defrost drain at the back of the fridge compartment is blocked. When the fridge cycles off, the ice melts but the water can't escape down the drain hole, so it backs up and spills onto the shelves above. Please check the back wall inside the fridge (usually near the bottom). Is there a small drain hole visible? If you can see it, try to clear any debris or ice gently with warm water from a squeezy bottle or a turkey baster. Let me know if that clears the blockage and stops the water returning.

ok yes theres a little groove and a hole at the bottom of the back wall and its got bits of lettuce and gunk in it. the water is only inside the fridge, nothing on the floor near the plug. how do i clear it out?

To clear it, switch the fridge off at the wall socket. Use a turkey baster or squeezy bottle to gently squirt warm (not boiling) water into that hole until it flows freely through. If there's solid gunk, you can carefully push a flexible pipe cleaner or a piece of soft tubing down the drain to break it up—do not use sharp objects like knives. Once clear, leave the fridge off for an hour with towels underneath to let any standing water drain out and the compartment dry completely before switching it back on.
ok will give it a go with a cotton bud and some warm water, i havent got a baster. should i leave the fridge off for an hour like you said? the food is all in there so might it go warm

[Heading: Likely cause: drain hose]
You don't need to leave it off for an hour if you have food in there; keeping it running is better for your groceries. Just clear the drain hole gently with the warm water and cotton bud now. Once that's done, keep an eye on it over the next few hours to see if the water stops returning. To help me confirm if any parts might be needed later, could you check the inside of the fridge for a sticker with the brand and model number? It's usually on a side wall or near the salad drawers.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
ok found the sticker, its a Beko and the model says CFG1582W. will do the cotton bud and warm water now and see if the water stops comming back

[Heading: Likely cause: drain hose]
Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. That sounds like the right approach. A cotton bud is fine for clearing out that gunk and lettuce bits—just be gentle so you don't push it further down or scratch the plastic. Since you have food inside, keeping the fridge running while you clear the drain is perfectly safe and better for your groceries. Once you've cleared the hole with warm water and a cotton bud, keep an eye on the area under the salad drawers for the next few hours. If the water stops appearing, it was just that blockage. If it keeps coming back despite the drain being clear, let me know and we can check if there are other issues like a door seal problem.

ok did it with the cotton bud and warm water and the water went straight down the hole no problem. youve said both to unplug it and to leave it running tho, i left it running with the food in. its been a few days now and no more water pooling under the draws

[Heading: Likely cause: drain hose]
To help prevent this from happening again in future, try to avoid placing items like loose lettuce leaves right against the back wall of the fridge compartment; keeping them slightly forward allows air and moisture to flow freely towards the drain. If you notice any water returning or if the freezer starts icing up excessively, let me know, but otherwise your Beko should be running perfectly now.
